summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis presented with left arm pain due to worsening steal syndrome in his left brachiocephalic arteriovenous fistula. He underwent elective fistula banding the following day, which was successful in reducing blood flow to alleviate symptoms while preserving access function. He remained asymptomatic postoperatively with no neurovascular deficits. His potassium was elevated at 6.4 on admission but decreased after an extended hemodialysis session. He tolerated a regular diet, maintained baseline functional status, and was discharged in stable condition to an extended care facility. Follow-up was arranged with transplant surgery and sleep medicine. Home medications were resumed, and discharge instructions included monitoring for arm symptoms, weight changes, and dialysis access issues.
